onboarding.title: Getting around this page
onboarding.description: A short map of the settings: what each block is for.
onboarding.data: Market data sources connect with your own keys. Tinkoff (MOEX), Alpaca and Business Quant (US stocks) need an API key from your broker account; Binance (crypto) and Yahoo (instrument profiles and logos) work without one. More connected sources means more tickers available to subscribe to.
onboarding.channels: Alert channels: the Telegram bot is the main one - put the token from @BotFather into its card, restart, then link your chat on the Notifications tab (one chat per account). Web Push delivers alerts to this browser; Email (SMTP) is reserved for a future channel; WhatsApp is for Meta business messaging and stays off until you turn it on.
onboarding.alerts: Alerts themselves live on the instruments and subscriptions pages - rules, pauses, trigger history. The bot's menu manages the same alerts from your phone.
onboarding.restart: Provider toggles and keys are stored to the database but applied when the app restarts. The amber warning icon marks changes that are waiting for a restart.

items.text: Combine conditions with AND/OR and nest groups inside groups: (RSI below 30 AND a volume spike) OR MACD crossing the signal line - the alert fires on any branch.

steps.title: Three steps to your first alert

items.title: Run the container
items.text: docker compose up with a password in the .env file - the app, Postgres and Redis come up together.

items.title: Add your keys
items.text: Settings → Providers: connect Tinkoff, Alpaca, Binance or Business Quant with your own API key and test the connection.

items.text: Pick an indicator, set the condition, choose the channels - Telegram, web push, Discord or a webhook.

gallery.title: What an alert looks like
gallery.subtitle: This is exactly what the engine draws when a rule fires: candles, the indicator overlay and an arrow on the candle that triggered - rendered from synthetic data, not a market feed. Switch charts with the arrows or a swipe, open one in full screen to inspect it.
